Diversity and Concentration of the Catch

Source: R/diversity_concentration.R
diversity_concentration.Rd

This function computes, for each year:

  • the number of species reported (items identified to species with catch) and the number of countries with catch;

  • the Shannon diversity index of the catch over FAO species items, \(H = -\sum p_i \ln p_i\), where \(p_i\) is the share of item \(i\);

  • the Herfindahl-Hirschman index (HHI) of species items and of countries, the sum of squared percentage shares (0 to 10 000; above 2 500 is usually read as highly concentrated);

  • the share of the top_n largest species items and countries.

Usage

diversity_concentration(
  area_data,
  top_n = 5,
  plot = TRUE,
  table = TRUE,
  lang = NULL,
  pptx = getOption("faofishingreport.pptx", FALSE),
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

area_data

FAO catch data: fishing_area_data()$area_data, or any subset of load_fao_data() (e.g. one country, or several fishing areas).

top_n

The number of largest species and countries for the top share. Default is 5.

plot

A logical value. If TRUE (default), charts are saved in figures/png/summary/.

table

A logical value. If TRUE (default), tables are saved in tables/.

lang

The language of the chart text and names: "en" (English), "zh" (Chinese) or "both" (Chinese and English). Default is NULL, which uses the language set with fao_settings() ("en" unless changed).

pptx

A logical value. If TRUE, charts are also saved as editable PowerPoint files in figures/pptx/summary/. Default is FALSE, which can be changed for all functions with fao_settings(pptx = TRUE).

label

The name used in the output file names. Default is the fishing area (or the country) of the data.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row per year.

See also

Other summary analyses: area_overview(), coastal_distant(), country_group_summary(), data_quality(), peak_trend(), regime_shift(), species_group_composition(), stock_status()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central", plot = FALSE)
diversity_concentration(FAO34$area_data, lang = "zh")
} # }
